summary: The checked-out Rust TreeCore was faster than Python in an alternating-order GPU-backed cache benchmark and in two independent, reverse-order tiny-Llama streaming server sessions at concurrency 8 and 64. No issue-specific production correction was justified.

tests.command: cargo test --locked --release (with LIBTORCH_USE_PYTORCH=1, the prepared interpreter's Torch libraries, and the repository compatibility header)
tests.what_was_measured: Native Rust TreeCore correctness: 846 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

tests.command: alternating five-round run_all_benchmarks(num_seqs=1200, chunk_len=96, kv_size=180000, FULL, page_size=1, verify=True, match/lock/cache_finished)
tests.what_was_measured: GPU-backed TreeCore operation throughput and correctness. Rust median throughput exceeded Python by 129.7% for match, 486.0% for lock/unlock, and 59.3% for cache_finished.

tests.command: run_server_benchmark.py twice per backend in python,rust,rust,python order; three rounds each at concurrency 8 and 64
tests.what_was_measured: Actual HTTP streaming and engine execution using the qualified deterministic tiny Llama. After excluding each level's first compilation/warmup round, Rust median e2e/TTFT/stream-span were respectively 6.6%/4.3%/2.1% lower at concurrency 8 and 2.3%/3.7%/2.3% lower at concurrency 64. Every request returned HTTP 200 with 12 streaming events.
Syntax validity of the retained fixture and benchmark runners.
Post-test cleanup: 0% GPU use and 0% allocated VRAM.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. Four real SGLang server processes executed streaming requests; server logs identify the Python and Rust TreeCore classes.

remaining_limitations: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct weights were unavailable; the random tiny Llama cannot validate Qwen semantics or the qwen tool-call parser.
The assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) is not the reported RTX 4090, so the original GPU-specific end-to-end result remains unverified.
The tiny fixture covered concurrency 8 and 64, not 256, and validates transport and engine execution only.
Each server's first round showed compilation/warmup transients and was excluded according to a declared rule; four post-warmup rounds per backend remain too small for a broad performance claim.
Server shutdown required SIGKILL after the runner's 30-second graceful timeout, but the subreaper removed descendants and ROCm reported no remaining GPU allocation.
